message.content:
For a fair (unbiased) coin, the probability of landing on heads in a single flip is

\[
P(\text{heads}) = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5 \; \text{(or 50\%)}.
\]

This assumes the coin has two equally likely outcomes—heads or tails—and no bias toward either side. If the coin were biased, you would need the bias parameter (e.g., \(p\) for heads) to compute the probability.
